name: n1-v0.1-worker-unreachable

graded_by.test: core/internal/worker/version_test.go — a live v0.1 manifest: no hello, ping, timers, kill request or linger; its sessions are unreachable / protocol and outlive worker_heartbeat; POST /sessions answers 503 worker_unavailable
harness/rigs/n1-negative.sh — a frozen v0.1 worker under the v0.2 core: its session is unreachable / protocol, never killed, and creation is refused 503 while only v0.1 workers run

description: N-1, the negative case (phase-01: a v0.1 worker has no handshake at all, so it cannot demonstrate reattach; immortality §6.4: never silently killed). A restarted v0.2 core finds a live v0.1 worker — its manifest has no proto_version — under a v0.1 supervisor. It dials first, as v0.1 does: the peer is live, so it is not worker_lost. It sends it no hello, ping, timers, kill request or linger; its session is unreachable / protocol, input refused (decision 5.38), alive past worker_heartbeat. The session timers (idle, unattended) and owner and admin ends still apply and reach the worker as a v0.1 close_channel, since session model §14 rejects an unbounded orphan. The supervisor is addressed but never asked for a worker, so no new session lands on a v0.1 worker (O1); the operator drains these. The core neither reads nor records its output (decision 5.38; orchestrator DEFAULT, approval page): it dials each data socket once, to tell live from lost, and closes it unread.
